caption:
A new paper on Hugging Face Papers asks a question many teams skip: is complex agentic memory always needed? The authors tested Raw-RAG, a naive baseline with dense retrieval and reranking over raw history. It ranked first among the compared memory systems in six of seven benchmark-model settings across four benchmarks.

What I see in companies is the same pattern. The team adds a memory layer, an orchestration layer, another abstraction. Nobody tests a plain baseline first, and nobody measures whether the added complexity helps.

I faced this in production. For a building materials store in southern Brazil, I built an AI sales rep on WhatsApp. The ERP has 13,312 products and 136 different ways of writing the unit of measure. The AI never sees the catalog. A simple search answers in milliseconds and hands 8 results to the model. The whole flow has 9 nodes. 65 out of 65 real customer questions found the right product.

My rule: test the plain baseline, measure it, and only then add complexity.

Comment SDR and I'll DM you how I did it.

Sources: huggingface.co
